# Parking (Code of Practice) Act 2019

The Parking (Code of Practice) Act 2019 is an act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom concerning the establishment of a code of practice for parking providers.
History
In 2017/2018, the number of parking charges reached a record high of 5,650,000, compared to 4,710,000 in 2016/2017 and 499,000 in 2007/2008.
During the passage of the bill, ParkingEye pursued Nicholas Bowen for an  fine for overstaying the free two hour limit at Welcome Break Membury Services. Legal representatives of ParkingEye failed to turn up to court. According to ParkingEye, it did send a representative to court but was told that the case was not on the list of hearings. When the company was contacted later, it said it was "considering its options within the time limits set out by the court".
The bill was supported by the government.
Provisions
The act allows the government to introduce a statutory code of practice.
Implementation
The government introduced a code of practice under the act in 2022, but withdrew this after legal challenge by parking companies.
A non-statutory code of practice was introduced by the International Parking Community and the British Parking Association, the two DVLA-accredited trade associations that private parking operators must be members of to issue penalty charge notice to drivers. The RAC described this as lacking "teeth" and urged the government to introduce a new statutory code under the act.
In 2025, the government committed to introducing a new code of practice under the act.
Further developments
In 2021/2022, 8,600,000 parking tickets were issued.
